deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page opens §4 of the 1967 crystals lecture notes, after a 'puzzle' summary on the previous page. That summary proposed to combine (a) the cohomology of complexes of differential operators, (b) relative stratified structures and (c) Washnitzer–Monsky theory. §4 sets out to make (b) geometric by introducing 'stratifying topoi' alongside 'crystalline topoi'.

4.1 in modern terms. Let X → S be a morphism of schemes and F an O_X-module equipped with a stratification relative to S. Concretely, this is a compatible family of isomorphisms between the two pullbacks of F to the infinitesimal neighbourhoods of the diagonal in X×_S X, satisfying the cocycle condition. Equivalently, it is an action of the ring of differential operators of infinite order Diff_{X/S}.

Grothendieck rewrites this datum as follows. Consider:
- any S-morphism f : Y → X;
- any nilpotent thickening Y ⊂ Y' over S such that f extends, at least locally on Y', to f' : Y' → X.

The stratification gives isomorphisms f'_1^*F ≅ f'_2^*F for any two extensions f'_1, f'_2 of f. This holds because (f'_1, f'_2) : Y' → X×_S X factors, locally, through an infinitesimal neighbourhood of the diagonal. These isomorphisms form a transitive system: they satisfy the cocycle condition, matching the cocycle condition of the stratification.

So the system descends to a well-defined O_{Y'}-module F_{Y'} extending f^*F, with obvious functoriality in (Y, Y'). Equivalently, a stratification is the same as a coherent rule assigning to each such thickening an extension of F to Y'. Pullback compatibility under morphisms of thickenings makes these extensions isomorphisms.

The local-extendability condition is the key restriction. It is automatic when X/S is formally smooth, by the infinitesimal lifting property. Without it, the condition singles out a 'stratifying' site, which is in general smaller than the full infinitesimal site.

Grothendieck then announces a site 'ad hoc' to express this conveniently. The next page defines it: crystalline and stratifying sites and topoi. It shows that special sheaves of modules on the stratifying site are equivalent to stratified modules, and conjectures/states H_cris/strat(X/S, O) ≅ H_DR(X/S) in characteristic 0 for X smooth.

Purpose: replace the algebraic notion of stratification (or D-module structure) by sheaves on a site of thickenings. Cohomology of stratified modules then becomes topos cohomology, comparable to de Rham cohomology. This is the passage from Diff-modules to crystals.
errors: No mathematical error. Unlike the opens-U-of-X infinitesimal site of the published 'Crystals' paper, the objects here are arbitrary S-morphisms Y → X with thickenings Y' (a 'big' variant). This is fine, but such a site has no final object, as the next page notes.
Gap: the transitivity claim needs the two extensions f'_1, f'_2 to land, locally, in a finite-order neighbourhood of the diagonal. That is true because Y ⊂ Y' is nilpotent, but it is not spelled out.
Gap: the descent of the system to a single module on Y' when extensions exist only locally on Y' is also implicit, not argued.

ideas.what: A relative stratification of an O_X-module is equivalent to a functorial, transitive system of extensions of f^*F to infinitesimal thickenings Y' of S-schemes Y → X over which f locally extends.
ideas.modern_name: Stratifications = crystals on the infinitesimal/stratifying site (Grothendieck's infinitesimal site; Berthelot's equivalence between stratified modules and crystals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, IHES 1966 notes, publ. in Dix exposés 1968); developed by Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, LNM 407, 1974)
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes', Dix exposés sur la cohomologie des schémas (1968)

ideas.what: Local extendability of f to Y' as the defining condition of a 'stratifying' site, automatic when X/S is formally smooth, so that the stratifying site agrees with the infinitesimal site in the smooth case.
ideas.modern_name: Stratifying site versus infinitesimal site; the formal-smoothness lifting property
ideas.where_published: Possibly implicit in 'Crystals...' §4–5; explicit treatment of stratifications in Berthelot LNM 407 Ch. II

ideas.what: Plan to introduce an ad hoc site (stratifying/crystalline topos) whose special sheaves are the stratified modules.
ideas.modern_name: Crystalline/infinitesimal topos; crystals as Cartesian sheaves
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968)

deep.surprise_reason: This is the lecture-note version of material Grothendieck published in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' and Berthelot later systematized. The only mildly distinctive features are the 'big' site with arbitrary Y → X and the explicit local-extendability condition defining the stratifying site. Both are standard variants.
transcription_corrections: Line 'tels que f se prolonge en un [?] (localement au moins)': plausibly 'tels que f se prolonge (localement au moins) en f' : Y' → X'. The inserted word is unclear and possibly crossed out.

'On peut donc dire que la donnée d'une stratification revient à la donnée, pour les voisinages infinitésimaux Y' d'un Y →f X (sur S) ... d'un prolongement de F en un Module sur Y'': the scattered 'données' fragments belong to this reading.
The diagram has X ←f— Y, Y ⊂ Y' with f' : Y' → X, and X → S. The Y and Y' labels were struck through and rewritten, consistent with the correction X → Y in the text.
